import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# The dataset provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean seaborn style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and an axes object for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7)) # Set a good figure size for clarity

# Generate a scatter plot to visualize relationships between numerical features

# - x-axis: Megapixels (a key camera specification)
# - y-axis: Price (USD) (a key outcome variable)
# - hue: Brand (distinguish points by color)
# - style: Sensor Type (distinguish points by marker shape)
# - size: Weight (grams) (distinguish points by size, indicating physical bulk)

    data=df,
    x="megapixels",
    y="price_usd",
    hue="brand",
    style="sensor_type",
    size="weight_grams",
    sizes=(100, 800), # Define the range of point sizes
    palette="tab10",  # Use a distinct categorical color palette

)

plt.xlabel("Megapixels", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Price (USD)", fontsize=12)

plt.tight_layout()
